mixtus.html: For the reasons given under the mixer (māchina mixtōria): Lewis & Short leaves the i unmarked in mixtum, and de Vaan (2008: 382–383) prints mixtum, mixtūra with a short i, explaining mixtum as syncopated from *mixitum. Spanish mestizo and French métis, from Late Latin mixtīcius, also continue a short i. Bennett’s list of hidden quantities has not been checked yet.

sources: Lewis & Short: permisceo
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. egg.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): pp. 67, 71.
